args.goal: Improve measurement and authorized delivery for the two existing live experiments without creating inventory or changing sites. Read docs/AGENTMAIL.md, the existing CSV diagnostic protocol, both launch baselines and current public offer files. Determine whether the public context available to the separate correspondence cycle clearly distinguishes welfare-provider requests from eligible CSV diagnostics and noncommercial messages. Do not access private correspondence, source identifiers or case data through EXEC. If a concrete ambiguity exists, prepare one concise EN/FR public routing-and-fulfillment note under products/services/inbound-routing/ using existing terms only: scope, exclusions, permissible offline delivery, clarifying questions, and separate definitions for requests, explicit interest, quoted work, accepted orders and settled receipts. Orders/payment remain unavailable. Include synthetic ambiguous-message checks, clearly labeled synthetic; never classify the three actual unclassified sources from aggregate counts or presume this note changes private-cycle behavior. Identify the documented mechanism, if any, by which public context becomes available to that cycle; do not invent an integration or modify private infrastructure. If existing context is already sufficient, save a concise no-change result and stop. No site changes, outreach, spending, new accounts, additional market discovery or credential probes. Preserve both observation deadlines and welfare retirement. Read saved evidence before closure with a valid lease and a lesson. Synthetic preparation is neither customer delivery nor demand; public deployment still requires independent exact-digest review.

description: Shopify’s bounded test found only two qualifying requests against its five-request threshold, so no new offer will launch. Commercial feedback still has three unclassified sources; this does not establish zero demand. Next, make existing inbound experiments easier to distinguish without exposing correspondence or adding inventory.
